rationale: C06 plausibly supplied a reusable form for promulgating detailed regulations directly through a presidential directive: an opening provision prescribes regulations, assigns them to specified parts of the Code of Federal Regulations, and then reproduces the regulations as formally numbered sections. The child uses the same concrete drafting machinery for regulations governing executive orders and proclamations. C12 and C14 share that codified-regulation structure, but C06 has the closest operative introductory formulation. The relationship is more substantial than a shared generic administrative purpose because it concerns the distinctive packaging and incorporation of a regulatory code within the directive itself.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The following regulations shall govern the preparation, presentation, filing, and publication of Executive orders and proclamations, and shall constitute §§ 1.91 through 1.97 of Chapter I of Title 1 of the Code of Federal Regulations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby prescribe the following portions of the regulations governing the administration of Title I of the said Act, which shall constitute portions of Parts 621 to 627, inclusive, of Title 32, chapter VI, Code of Federal Regulations
shared_material.explanation: Both introduce the directive as a presidential prescription of regulations and expressly place the ensuing provisions into identified CFR titles, chapters, parts, or sections.

shared_material.child_excerpt: § 1.91 Form. ... § 1.92 Routing and approval of drafts. ... § 1.97 Proclamations of treaties excluded.
shared_material.explanation: Both follow the introductory incorporation clause with a substantial body of formally captioned, section-numbered regulatory text.
